did_you_know.text: The heading identifies the psalm as a psalm of David, intended to be performed with stringed instruments, and calls it a “maskil”—a title that also appears in other psalms.
The setting described in the psalm is the report by the Ziphites to Saul about David’s hiding place: “Is not David hiding among us?”
The request “Save me by your name” connects God’s name with salvation, while “In your might, vindicate me” expresses a request for judgment and a just decision.
This verse contains a twofold appeal to be heard: “O God, hear my prayer” and “Listen to the words of my mouth.” The repetition emphasizes the worshiper’s desire for his prayer to be heard.
Those opposing the speaker are described as “strangers” and “ruthless men,” and the moral reason for their behavior is given in the words: “They do not set God before them.”
Despite the threat, the speaker expresses confidence: “Surely God is my helper.” He also describes God as the one who sustains his life—“the Lord is the support of my soul.”
The speaker asks that evil return upon those who lie in wait for him—that is, his enemies—and entrusts their judgment to divine truth: “In your faithfulness, destroy them.”

The response he plans to make for his deliverance is an offering of thanks: “I will sacrifice a freewill offering to you” and “I will praise your name.” The phrase “freewill offering” emphasizes that the sacrifice is presented as a voluntary act.
At the end of the psalm, the speaker summarizes the reason for his thanks: he has been delivered “from every trouble,” and he says that he has seen his enemies’ defeat with his own eyes.
